items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Seems to me, Kit Howard plays that way now. I believe he does.

ctx.x: Well, I play it like this now. And that's the standard. Yeah. Now who plays around inside of the lip way today? I see somebody doing that not long ago.

Some of the trumpet players. I forgot who it was though. Seems to me, Kit Howard plays that way now. I believe he does. Maybe Kit Clayton, I can't remember. One of them, yeah, one of them. But you can't get no power like that. You can't put nothing behind it. I wonder why people started that way. I did. I started wrong by not having nobody to share. Of course, when I was in the army, a fellow named Lewis Mathis called him Chiff. He tried to get me away from that, but I, you know, wouldn't listen to him until I…
Oh, oh, oh. What are some of the other different ways that guys had of lipping their horns?

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1958-12-22
items.q: And he jumped up there and, you know, got on the truck and- And played with me.

ctx.x: Yeah, but I, no, no, Lee was here. He was playing on that story. Yeah. And anyway, so we got out there, the two trucks, and we tied up on 47 and I think in, where the Riggle Theater at? South Parkway. Well, 47 and South Parkway. South Parkway, man, they never seen something like that in all their life. Boy, we tied up like we did back there in the olden days. And Bill, did we have a ball? And that's when Punch, Punch Miller, well he had been up there pretty good while. Punch Miller, we call him Kid Punch right…
And he jumped up there and, you know, got on the truck and- And played with me.
Yeah, yep. Because Lee was really so much sad.

items.title: Avery "Kid" Howard Interview, 1961-05-22
items.q: Well I saw Punch when I was up there, Punch Miller.

ctx.x: time back. Were there any other New Orleans guys up there other than Louie?
Well I saw Punch when I was up there, Punch Miller. Yeah.
In fact I didn't get around.
